title: Wire dynamic HDR extraction into CPU encode
summary: Wired Dynamic HDR preserve_encode decisions into Do-Encode by resolving MKV video track IDs, extracting Dolby Vision/HDR10+ metadata, resolving x265-safe artifact paths, forcing CPU/libx265, and passing artifact parameters only to the CPU HDR encode plan.
reason: Dynamic HDR preservation had planning, extraction helpers, artifact-path guards, and policy routing but still stopped before runtime extraction/injection. Do-Encode needed backend-owned fail-closed wiring before output verification and real-media validation could proceed.
behavior_before: When Dynamic HDR policy selected preserve_encode, Do-Encode marked preservation as not ready and either blocked preserve_or_review sources or redirected preserve_or_remux sources to remux/drop behavior.
behavior_after: When preserve_encode is selected, Do-Encode resolves MKV track identity, extracts Dynamic HDR metadata, resolves relative x265 artifact paths, skips GPU attempts, runs CPU/libx265 from the artifact working directory, passes Dolby Vision/HDR10+ x265 parameters to the CPU plan only, and records preserve/drop/block evidence. preserve_or_review still blocks on extraction/path failures; preserve_or_remux still attempts guarded remux fallback before any lossy encode.
tests_added: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-DynamicHdrDetectionChecks.ps1 now asserts Do-Encode calls the Dynamic HDR track resolver, extraction executor, x265 path resolver, CPU-only artifact parameters, CPU working directory, distinct route reason, and no drop warning for preservation-ready encodes.
rollback_plan: Revert this packet to restore the previous fail-closed/not-ready Dynamic HDR preserve_encode behavior, remove the new static assertions, refresh generated summaries, and leave source media/runtime state untouched.
